**Udviklingsmål ≥ 90%** (Development Target ≥ 90%) is a standardized quality benchmark utilized in the Danish healthcare system to evaluate the treatment of patients with atrial fibrillation. Featured prominently in the annual "Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark" (*Atrieflimren i Danmark*) reports published by the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute, this threshold mandates that a minimum of 90% of specific patient cohorts must receive guideline-recommended care. Its primary application is for Indicator 1, which measures the proportion of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients who initiate anticoagulation therapy within 30 days. The benchmark is also applied to other quality indicators, such as treatment persistence and kidney function monitoring (Indicators 4a and 4b).

The performance against this ≥90% target varies significantly depending on the specific clinical indicator being evaluated. For Indicator 1 (timely initiation of anticoagulation), the national development target is successfully met [^src1]. At the cluster level, 17 out of 22 clusters achieve the ≥90% threshold, while the remaining five clusters report results narrowly missing the mark, ranging between 88% and 89% [^src1]. [[klynge-vest|Klynge VEST]] is among the clusters evaluated under this framework [^src1]. 

Conversely, when applied to Indicators 4a and 4b—which assess anticoagulation treatment persistence two years post-diagnosis and the monitoring of kidney function in patients on DOACs, respectively—the ≥90% target is not met at the national level, and results remain largely stagnant compared to previous years [^src2]. At the regional level for these specific indicators, only [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] manages to fulfill the ≥90% development target [^src2].
